problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Globally convex, G-Lipschitz functions on R^(m+1), with a global minimizer x* satisfying ||x*|| ≤ R. No differentiability or strong convexity is required.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Stochastic subgradient oracle: each query x returns g(x,ω), with E[g(x,ω)] = v(x) ∈ ∂f(x). Seeds are IID; function values are not supplied.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: The centered oracle has E||g(x,ω)-v(x)||² ≤ vTop + m vRest, implied by its directional exponential bounds.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: Euclidean geometry in dimension m+1, including m=0.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Known anisotropic sub-Gaussian proxy Σ = diag(vTop,vRest,…,vRest): E exp(t〈g-v,u〉) ≤ exp(t²〈u,Σu〉/2) for every x,u,t. Public parameters satisfy G,R,ε>0 and 0≤vRest≤vTop; the distinguished direction is coordinate 0. The objective, subgradient selection, and sampling law are hidden.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SpikedSubGaussianConvex.lean: varianceProxy; IsSubGaussianSubgradient; spec.Public, publicInput, valid, admissible

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: A measurable output x must satisfy f(x)-min f ≤ ε; no particular iterate or output construction is required.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: Failure probability P(f(output)-min f > ε) ≤ 1/3, under the joint algorithm and oracle randomness, with a fixed oracle-call budget.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The convex Lipschitz stochastic subgradient formulation is classical, but the specified public spiked directional sub-Gaussian proxy is a specialized anisotropic noise assumption.

descriptionHtml:
Convex Minimization with Spiked Noise

We consider minimizing a convex, G-Lipschitz function f:E→R on E=Rm+1, where m≥0 is an integer and G>0. A global minimizer x⋆ satisfies ∥x⋆∥≤R, where R>0. The oracle returns an unbiased subgradient estimate with independent, identically distributed samples and centered sub-Gaussian noise: its variance proxy is vtop along the first coordinate and vrest in orthogonal directions, where 0≤vrest≤vtop. For ε>0, the goal is a measurable output x¯∈E satisfying f(x¯)−f(x⋆)≤ε with probability at least 2/3 over the algorithm and oracle randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈Ef(x). We use the Euclidean inner product and norm, and index coordinates by 0,…,m. The algorithm receives m, the measurable sample space Ω, and G,R,vtop,vrest,ε; the objective and oracle distribution are accessible only through oracle replies.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Convexity and Lipschitz continuity). For every x,y∈E and s∈[0,1], f((1−s)x+sy)≤(1−s)f(x)+sf(y),|f(x)−f(y)|≤G∥x−y∥.

Assumption 2 (Bounded minimizer). There exists x⋆∈E such that f(x⋆)≤f(x)for every x∈E,∥x⋆∥≤R.

Assumption 3 (Spiked sub-Gaussian subgradient oracle). There are a probability measure p on Ω, a map v:E→E, and a jointly measurable map g:E×Ω→E. For every x∈E, the map g(x,⋅) is Bochner integrable under p, and Eξ∼p[g(x,ξ)]=v(x),⟨v(x),y−x⟩≤f(y)−f(x)(y∈E). Define the directional variance proxy by V(u)=vrest∥u∥2+(vtop−vrest)u02,u∈E. For every x,u∈E and t∈R, the random variable exp⁡(t⟨g(x,ξ)−v(x),u⟩) is integrable under ξ∼p and satisfies Eξ∼p[exp⁡(t⟨g(x,ξ)−v(x),u⟩)]≤exp⁡(t2V(u)2). The sample sequence (ξk)k≥0 has a probability law Q on ΩN under which its coordinate maps are measurable, mutually independent, and each has distribution p. At call k, a query x∈E receives g(x,ξk). The algorithm’s randomness is independent of this sample sequence.

Queries may be made anywhere in E. After the allotted oracle calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and satisfy P(f(x¯)−f(x⋆)>ε)≤13, where P is the joint law of the algorithm’s randomness and the oracle sample sequence.

comparisonHtml:
Convex, globally G-Lipschitz f:Rd→R has a global minimizer ∥x⋆∥≤R; G,R,ε>0. Fresh IID samples from a probability measure p feed a jointly measurable, integrable oracle g, with ∫g(x,ω)dp=v(x)∈∂f(x). For every x,u,t, the exponential moment is integrable and at most exp⁡(t2[vrest∥u∥2+(vtop−vrest)u02]/2) for ⟨g−v,u⟩, where 0≤vrest≤vtop and the spike direction is known. Target: measurable x^ with P{f(x^)−f(x⋆)>ε}≤1/3.

Comparison for SpikedSubGaussianConvex.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) SpikedSubGaussianSoftCutConvex (Ours) (⋆⋆) (review) O((d+τR2/ε2)ℓ5)
(2) ESGO cutting planes (Marsden et al. 2025), Cor. 3 O((d+dvtopR2/ε2)ℓO(1)) (1): noise coefficient τ instead of dvtop; gain up to d when anisotropy dominates logarithms. For G=R=1, ε=vtop=d−1, vrest=d−3: O(dlog5⁡d) versus O(d2logO(1)⁡d). (1) needs a known spike and sub-Gaussian MGF; (2) allows directional sub-exponential tails. Isotropic noise gives no polynomial gain.
(3) SGD, derived probability bound (Marsden et al. 2025), §1 O(1+(G2+τ)R2/ε2) (1) removes G2R2/ε2, adding dℓ5; wins if G2R2/ε2≫max{d,τR2/ε2}ℓ5. In (2)’s example: O(dlog5⁡d) versus O(d2). (1) requires known-spike sub-Gaussian noise; (3) needs only finite variance and avoids ℓ5. (3) is cheaper when G2R2/ε2≲d.

Abbr: d=m+1, τ=vtop+(d−1)vrest, ℓ=1+log⁡(d(1+GR/ε)). Costs count individual stochastic subgradient calls, including batches. ℓO(1) denotes the polylogarithmic factors suppressed in the cited bound. ESGO: sub-exponential stochastic gradient oracle, here with scale σE≍dvtop. SGD: stochastic gradient descent; its expected-error bound uses E∥g∥2≤G2+τ, converted by Markov’s inequality.

Marsden, Annie, Liam O’Carroll, Aaron Sidford, and Chenyi Zhang. 2025. Isotropic Noise in Stochastic and Quantum Convex Optimization. https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2510.20745.

import LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Measure.Haar.InnerProductSpace

open MeasureTheory
open scoped RealInnerProductSpace

namespace LongTails.Setups.SpikedSubGaussianConvex

open OracleTemplate

structure Params where
  m : ℕ
  Ω : Type
  [measurableΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω]
  G : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  vTop : ℝ
  vRest : ℝ
  ε : ℝ

attribute [instance] Params.measurableΩ

abbrev Space (q : Params) := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (q.m + 1))

noncomputable def varianceProxy (q : Params) (u : Space q) : ℝ :=
  q.vRest * ‖u‖ ^ 2 + (q.vTop - q.vRest) * (u 0) ^ 2

structure IsSubGaussianSubgradient (q : Params) (p : Measure q.Ω)
    [IsProbabilityMeasure p] (f : Space q → ℝ) (v : Space q → Space q)
    (g : Space q → q.Ω → Space q) : Prop where
  measurable : Measurable (Function.uncurry g)
  integrable : ∀ x, Integrable (g x) p
  unbiased : ∀ x, (∫ ω, g x ω ∂p) = v x
  support : ∀ x y, ⟪v x, y - x⟫ ≤ f y - f x
  exponential_integrable : ∀ x u t,
    Integrable (fun ω => Real.exp (t * ⟪g x ω - v x, u⟫)) p
  exponential_bound : ∀ x u t,
    (∫ ω, Real.exp (t * ⟪g x ω - v x, u⟫) ∂p) ≤
      Real.exp (t ^ 2 * varianceProxy q u / 2)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Params
  Public := Params
  Instance q := Space q → ℝ
  Query q := Space q
  Reply q := Space q
  Output q := Space q
  publicInput q := q
  valid q := 0 < q.G ∧ 0 < q.R ∧ 0 ≤ q.vRest ∧ q.vRest ≤ q.vTop ∧ 0 < q.ε
  admissible q f O :=
    ∃ (v : Space q → Space q) (g : Space q → q.Ω → Space q)
      (p : ProbabilityMeasure q.Ω) (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → q.Ω)),
    StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
      (fun k (ξ : ℕ → q.Ω) => ξ k) (p : Measure _) (P : Measure _) ∧
    O = { Seed := fun _ => q.Ω
          law := P
          answer := fun _ (_, x) seed => g x seed } ∧
    ConvexOn ℝ Set.univ f ∧
    (∀ x y, |f x - f y| ≤ q.G * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    (∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧ ‖xstar‖ ≤ q.R) ∧
    IsSubGaussianSubgradient q (p : Measure _) f v g
  successful q f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧ ∃ xstar, IsMinOn f Set.univ xstar ∧
      (P : Measure _) {ω | q.ε < f (output ω) - f xstar} ≤ (1 / 3 : ENNReal)

end LongTails.Setups.SpikedSubGaussianConvex
